licenses.text:
Darby Unrevidierte Elberfelder, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/deuelo/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation):
> "Public Domain
Language: Deutsch (German, Standard)
Translation by: Julius Anton von Poseck, Carl Brockhaus, and John Nelson Darby"
(from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/deuelo/copyright.htm)

Why this is public domain:
Translators: Julius Anton Eugen von Poseck, 1816-1896 (died in Lewisham, London, United Kingdom); Carl Friedrich Wilhelm Brockhaus, 1822-1899 (died in Elberfeld, Germany); John Nelson Darby, 1800-1882 (died 1882, United Kingdom). First publication of this text: 1905, Elberfeld, Germany (eBible's title: 'The Holy Bible in German, Unrevised Elberfelder 1905'). US: published in 1905, before 1931, so public domain in the United States. Origin country: Germany and the United Kingdom. Germany's rule is life plus 70 years (German Urheberrechtsgesetz section 64): Brockhaus's term ended in 1969 and Poseck's in 1967. The United Kingdom's life plus 70 years ended for Darby in 1953 and for Poseck in 1967. Every translator died in 1899 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 120 years or less, whatever the exact rule of Germany or the United Kingdom.

Sources of these facts:
eBible.org copyright page (https://ebible.org/deuelo/copyright.htm) and details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=deuelo); life dates from German Wikipedia (https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Anton_von_Poseck and https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Brockhaus) and English Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Nelson_Darby).

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-deuelo-ffd33bd5, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
